definitions.explanation: A country at the southern tip of the African continent, known for its diverse population, mineral wealth (especially gold and diamonds), and the history of apartheid and its end.

examples.japanese: {南|みなみ}アフリカ⟦へ→へ：02473_he⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧。
{南|みなみ}アフリカ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦ダイヤモンド→ダイヤモンド：11038_daiyamondo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{産地|さんち}→産地：04031_sanchi⟧として⟦{有名|ゆうめい}→有名：01106_yuumei⟧だ。
examples.english: South Africa is famous as a producer of diamonds.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{頃|ころ}、⟦{家族|かぞく}→家族：00552_kazoku⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{南|みなみ}アフリカ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{旅行|りょこう}→旅行：00748_ryokou⟧したことがある。
examples.english: When I was a child, I once traveled to South Africa with my family.

notes:
{南|みなみ}アフリカ is a country at the southern tip of the African continent, home to major cities such as ヨハネスブルグ and ケープタウン, and famous internationally for its diamond and gold mines.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {南|みなみ}アフリカ⟦{共和国|きょうわこく}→共和国：24322_kyouwakoku⟧: the Republic of South Africa (formal name)
- {南|みなみ}アフリカ{産|さん}: made in South Africa
- {南|みなみ}アフリカ⟦{人|じん}→〜人：09849_jin⟧: a South African (person)

CULTURAL NOTE:
{南|みなみ}アフリカ ended its アパルトヘイト policy of racial segregation in 1994, when ネルソン・マンデラ became its first Black president - a historical turning point often mentioned in Japanese media.
